title: Custom Redux Hooks
description: Learn how to create custom hooks for reusable Redux logic, including patterns for authentication, lists, and async actions.

data.text: Custom hooks are the React-idiomatic way to **encapsulate and reuse** Redux logic across many components. Instead of repeating `useSelector` and `useDispatch` calls in every component that needs the same data or actions, you build one hook that returns a clean API.

data.title: Why Custom Hooks?
data.text: A custom hook is just a JavaScript function whose name starts with `use`. It can call other hooks inside it and return any value you want — state, derived data, or action dispatchers.

Imagine five components that all need to read the current user and dispatch `logout`. Without custom hooks, every component repeats the same `useSelector` and `useDispatch` calls — and any change to that logic has to be applied in five places.

data.title: Repeated boilerplate

data.text: Let's build `useAuth`. It returns the user, an `isAuthenticated` boolean, a guard function, and a `logout` action — everything a component needs in one call.

data.title: Three ways to reuse Redux logic

cards.title: Custom Hook
cards.description: Plain function that calls `useSelector`/`useDispatch`. Returns any shape you want.
pros: Zero nesting — just call and destructure

cards.title: Higher-Order Component
cards.description: Wraps a component, passing store data as props.
cons: Adds extra nesting (prop drilling through wrappers)

cards.title: Render Props
cards.description: Component accepts a function as a child and calls it with store data.
pros: Very flexible — full control of render

terms.definition: A JavaScript function starting with `use` that may call other hooks and returns any value.
Only call hooks at the top level and from React functions or other hooks.
Hiding internal Redux calls behind a clean API so components don't need to know about selectors or action creators.
A function that reads a slice of Redux state. Often passed to `useSelector`.

items: Keep hooks focused — one hook, one concern (auth, cart, form)
Return a stable, predictable shape (object with named keys)
Memoize functions returned from hooks with `useCallback` if passed to memoized children
Place hooks in a `src/hooks/` or `src/features/<feature>/hooks/` directory

data.title: Naming
data.text: Always prefix with `use`. React will refuse to call your function if it doesn't follow this convention.

data.title: Build a `useTodos` hook
data.description:
Create a custom hook called `useTodos` that:
1. Reads the todos list from the store with `useSelector`.
2. Returns `{ todos, addTodo, toggleTodo, removeTodo }`.
3. The action functions should be wrapped in `useCallback` so they can be safely passed to memoized children.
4. Write a tiny test with `renderHook` that confirms the hook returns an array.
steps: Use `useDispatch()` once at the top of the hook.
`renderHook(() => useTodos())` returns a `result` you can read.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Custom hooks encapsulate Redux reads and dispatches behind a clean API
They replace HOCs and render props for modern React codebases
One hook can be imported by many components, keeping logic DRY
data.takeaway: Custom hooks organize and reuse Redux logic in a React-native way.
